promptState.text: Keep the woman, her pose and the framing of <image1> exactly as they are, and dress her in the black PIXA t-shirt and the blue jeans from <image2>. Keep her face, hair and body shape, the original background and the original lighting. The clothes fit naturally, with realistic fabric texture and natural folds. High fashion editorial photography, sharp details.

{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt and looks at your pictures.
  • Load VAE - Turns pictures into the model's own format and back. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can hand back a transparent picture.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Load Image - Character - The picture you are editing. In the prompt it is <image1>.
  • 2. Load Image - Outfit - A second picture the model can take things from. In the prompt it is <image2>. Its loader scales it to about 1 megapixel, the size the model reads it at.
  • 3. Pick Orientation and Size - The size and shape of the result. Picture 1 always goes to the model whole. Pick the shape closest to it (the demo picture is 9:16, so 768 x 1376) and the result lines up with it in the Compare; pick another shape and the model re-frames the picture to fit it. The starred sizes are Qwen's native 2K ones and much slower.
  • 4. Add a prompt - What to change, and what to keep. Name the pictures as <image1> and <image2>.
  • 5. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same result, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The speed nodes

Teal, above the graph.

  • Qwen Image 2.1 Cache - Where the model keeps what it has already worked out about your pictures and the prompt, so it does not redo that on every step. Leave it on auto / default. The note on the right says when to change it.
  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves.

  • Math Expression - Works out how many megapixels the size from step 3 has, so picture 1 is read at the same number of pixels as the result.
  • Scale Image to Total Pixels - Works out the size picture 1 is read at: that many pixels, in steps of 32, in picture 1's own shape. Only that size is used.
  • Get Image Size - Reads that size as a width and a height for Resize Crop Pixaroma under it.
  • Resize Crop Pixaroma - Scales picture 1 to that size and trims the few pixels that do not fit, so the model gets the whole picture and nothing is stretched.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads your prompt and both pictures. Its resolution is set to 0, which takes the pictures as they come: picture 1 from the helpers, picture 2 at about 1 megapixel from its loader. Its negative prompt box does nothing at CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so leave it empty.
  • Empty Latent Image - The blank canvas for the result, at the size from step 3. The encoder's own canvas would always copy picture 1's shape.
  • KSampler - The render: 25 steps, euler, simple, CFG 1, the settings from ComfyUI's own template.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Image Compare Pixaroma - Picture 1, as the model saw it, and the result, one over the other. Move the mouse across it to slide between them.
  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the result and saves it to your output folder as a PNG.

The dark Run Timer above them shows how long the last Run took.

", "buttonColor": "#f66744", "lineColor": "#f66744", "width": 720, "height": 1363, "backgroundColor": "#2a2a2a"}

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this workflow makes

An edited version of picture 1, following your prompt. Picture 2 is a reference the model can take things from: here, the outfit. The result is the size you pick in step 3.

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 How long a Run takes

SizePixelsNew pictures or promptNew seed only
768 x 1376about 1 MP, the demo's 9:1612 s10 s
1536 x 1536about 2.4 MP, square27 s22 s
1536 x 2752native 2K, 9:1658 s47 s

Change a picture or the prompt and the model reads both pictures again, which is the first time column. Change only the seed and it reuses what it read, which is the second.

The size is what costs you: native 2K took about five times as long as the 1 MP size. Try your prompt at a 1 MP size and go up once you like the result.

 Picking the size

Picture 1 always goes to the model whole, read at the same number of pixels as the result. Pick the shape closest to it and the result lines up with it in the Compare. Pick another shape and the model re-frames the picture to fit. On this 9:16 demo, square kept her whole head on 8 of 8 seeds: on 6 she stayed the size she is in the original, with more background at the sides, and on 2 the model framed her a little closer. Landscape framed her from the head to about the knees on 4 of 4.

 Kitchen attention

The teal Model Attention Backend node is set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the attention maths. On the same seed at 1536 x 2752, it took 47 s, against 1 min 16 s with the normal pytorch attention, and the two pictures came out the same, with small differences in the fine details. To compare it yourself, switch the node to pytorch attention.

It needs an Nvidia or AMD graphics card. On anything else ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself, so the workflow still runs.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI has to load 6.8 GB of image model and 8.7 GB of text encoder. Measured on a 768 x 1376 edit: 15 s with the models unloaded first, 9 s once they were loaded.

That was with the model files still in this machine's file cache. The very first load after switching the computer on reads them off the disk for real and will be slower; that case was not measured, so no number is given for it.

 What it takes off the card

The graphics card peaked at about 21 GB during these runs, at 1536 x 1536. ComfyUI keeps the models loaded while it has room, so that number says a 24 GB card copes, not how little the model can get by with.

 The memory node (Qwen Image 2.1 Cache)

While it renders, the model keeps what it has worked out about your pictures and your prompt in a cache, so it does not redo that on every step. The teal node says where that cache lives. Leave it on auto / default: auto keeps the cache in spare graphics memory and moves it to system RAM when that runs out.

On a smaller card, if an edit is slow, try dtype int8. It halves the cache, and the node's own description says that can speed an edit up when memory is short. On this 24 GB card it made no difference (48 s against 47 s at native 2K). Setting device to cpu, which keeps the cache in system RAM all the time, also cost nothing here (47 s).

 Writing the prompt

Name the pictures as <image1> and <image2>, and say what should stay the same as well as what should change.

Keep the framing. When picture 2 has something that is outside picture 1's frame, the model tends to zoom out to fit it in. Tested on a waist-up photo with an outfit picture that includes boots: asking for the jeans and the boots gave a full-body shot in 5 of 6 tries. Asking only for the t-shirt and the jeans, and to keep the framing of <image1>, cut that to 1 of 7. The demo outfit has no boots, and with the demo prompt the framing held in all 8 tries.

More pictures. The model takes up to 10 reference pictures. Plug another Load Image Mini into the next free image slot on Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1, which appears as soon as the one before it is used, and name it in the prompt as <image3>. Picture 1 is always the one being edited. Workflows 5, 6 and 7 come set up with 3, 4 and 6 pictures.

", "buttonColor": "#f66744", "lineColor": "#f66744", "width": 810, "height": 1407, "backgroundColor": "#2a2a2a"}
